extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic/anabelian geometry and specialists in Mochizuki's IUT theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, structural properties, and group-theoretic reconstruction criteria for tempered fundamental groups, temperoids, and associated semi-graphs of anabelioids for hyperbolic curves (used in IUT-style arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempered group
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall refer to (… ) as a tempered group (Note that any pro-finite group is a tempered group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'tempered group' is used throughout as the basic topological group object; pro-finite groups form a special case. Many constructions (Btemp, tempered fundamental group) are defined relative to a tempered group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temp-slim
rubrics_metrics.description: We say that G is temp-slim if we have Z_G(H) = {1} for any open subgroup H ≤ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temp-slimness is a strong centralizer-triviality condition: the centralizer in G of every open subgroup is trivial. Used to control conjugacy/centralizer phenomena in tempered fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatively temp-slim (over a target via f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f : G1 → G2 be a continuous homomorphism of tempered groups. We say G1 is relatively temp-slim over G2 (via f) if Z_{G2}(Im f(H)) = {1} for any open subgroup H ≤ G1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A relative version of temp-slim controlling centralizers of images of open subgroups in the target; used when comparing tempered groups via homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Btemp / B constructions and connected temperoid / anabelioid
rubrics_metrics.description: For a topological group G, Btemp(G) (resp. B(G)) is the category whose objects are countable discrete sets (resp. finite sets) with a continuous G-action, and whose morphisms are morphisms of G-sets. A category C is a connected temperoid (resp. a connected anabelioid) if C is equivalent to Btemp(G) (resp. B(G)) for a tempered group G (resp. a pro-finite group G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connected temperoids/anabelioids are the categorical avatars of (tempered / pro-finite) groups; when C ≃ Btemp(G) and G has countable basis one can reconstruct G up to inner automorphism by the same method as Galois categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of temperoids/anabelioids
rubrics_metrics.description: For connected temperoids (resp. anabelioids) C1, C2, a morphism C1 → C2 is an isomorphism class of functors C2 → C1 which preserves finite limits and countable colimits (resp. finite colimits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This categorical notion of morphism matches the group-theoretic continuous outer homomorphisms under the equivalences below; note small definitional differences referenced in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence between outer homomorphisms and category morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If G1, G2 are tempered groups with countable basis (resp. pro-finite groups), then there are natural bijections among (i) the set of continuous outer homomorphisms G1 → G2, (ii) the set of morphisms Btemp(G1) → Btemp(G2) (resp. B(G1) → B(G2)), and (iii) the set of morphisms of the 0th-level categories Btemp(G1)^0 → Btemp(G2)^0 (resp. B(G1)^0 → B(G2)^0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the categorical ↔ group-theoretic dictionary used to pass between functors of temperoids/anabelioids and continuous outer homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual semi-graph GX for a pointed stable curve
rubrics_metrics.description:
Let X be a pointed stable curve over k with marked points D; write X := X 
 D. The dual semi-graph GX has vertices the irreducible components of X, closed edges the nodes of X, and open edges the marked points D. A closed edge e connects vertices v and v' iff the node corresponding to e is the intersection of branches corresponding to X_v and X_{v'}; an open edge connects the vertex containing the marked point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the combinatorial dual (semi-)graph attached to the special fibre of a stable curve; later constructions attach Galois/anabelioid data to this underlying semi-graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro-(S) semi-graph of anabelioids (G_v, G_e, G_ex)
rubrics_metrics.description: To each vertex v of GX attach G_v = the Galois category (connected anabelioid) of finite étale coverings of X_v^0 of (S)-power degree tamely ramified along nodes and marked points; to each closed edge e attach G_e similarly for the local node (non-canonically Spec k((t))); to each open edge ex attach G_ex for the marked point. For each edge there are natural pullback functors G_{v} → G_e, and the data G_v, G_e, and these functors define a (pro-(S)) semi-graph of anabelioids G_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This upgrades the combinatorial dual semi-graph by Galois/anabelioid categories at vertices and edges; it is the fundamental object whose associated B(G) produces admissible/tempered coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B(G) of a semi-graph of anabelioids
rubrics_metrics.description: For a semi-graph of anabelioids G = {G_v, G_e, G_v → G_e} with connected underlying semi-graph, B(G) is the category whose objects are data {S_v, σ_e} with S_v an object of G_v and σ_e an isomorphism in G_e between the images of the neighboring S_v; morphisms are natural. B(G) is a Galois category (or connected anabelioid); its fundamental group is the admissible fundamental group of X in the geometric situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B(G) glues local covering data into global admissible coverings; the fundamental group π1(B(G)) captures the admissible (pro-(S)) fundamental group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Bcov(G) and temperoid Btemp(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bcov(G) extends B(G) to coverings dominated by graph coverings; Btemp(G) is the full subcategory of Bcov(G) whose objects become countable coproducts when restricted to each local G_c after being split by some S^0 coming from B(G). We refer to Btemp(G) as the (pro-(S)) (connected) temperoid associated with G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Btemp(G) isolates those coverings that are 'tempered' (countable-type) rather than finite; Btemp is the categorical source for defining the tempered fundamental group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempered fundamental group π1^temp(Btemp(G)) and remarks on pro-(S) quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: One can associate π1^temp := π1(Btemp(G)) (after choosing a fiber functor). π1((S);temp) is not the maximal pro-(S) quotient of π1(B(G)) since the profinite completion of the 'graph covering portion' need not be pro-(S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care: the tempered π1 mixes profinite (pro-(S)) and discrete/combinatorial parts; the graph-covering/combinatorial portion can obstruct a simple pro-(S) quotient description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of π1^temp(X) as inverse limit of admissible fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an exhaustive sequence of open characteristic subgroups N_i of π1^temp(X), each N_i corresponds to a finite log-étale covering whose special fibre determines a semi-graph G_i of anabelioids. There are compatible functors Btemp(G_i) → Btemp(G) and surjections π1^temp(Btemp(G_i)) → π1^temp(Btemp(G)), and π1^temp(X) = lim_i π1^temp(G_i) (with analogous expression for π1(X) as pro-finite limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inverse-limit description reduces properties of the tempered fundamental group of the generic fibre to properties of admissible fundamental groups of special fibres; used repeatedly (see Lemma 6.4, Corollary 6.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verticial and edge-like subgroups (Definition 6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a semi-graph of anabelioids G, a verticial subgroup is a subgroup of the form π1(G_v) (viewed in π1^temp(G)); an edge-like subgroup is a subgroup of the form π1(G_e) for a closed edge e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These canonical subgroups correspond to vertex/edge local fundamental groups in the tempered fundamental group and are the basic building blocks for group-theoretic reconstruction of the dual graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic characterisation of verticial and edge-like subgroups (Proposition 6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The maximal compact subgroups of π1^temp(G) are precisely the verticial subgroups. (2) The nontrivial intersection of two maximal compact subgroups are precisely the edge-like subgroups of π1^temp(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These purely group-theoretic criteria allow reconstruction of the dual graph (vertices/closed edges) from π1^temp without using Galois action; see Remark 6.6.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: compact-conjugation forces tempered membership (Proposition 6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a smooth hyperbolic log-curve and π1^temp(G) its tempered group; let H ⊂ π1(G) be a nontrivial compact subgroup and γ ∈ π1(G) an element such that γ H γ^{-1} ⊂ π1^temp(G). Then γ ∈ π1^temp(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roughly: an element of the profinite completion that conjugates a nontrivial compact subgroup into the tempered subgroup must itself lie in the tempered subgroup. Proof uses tempered vertices in the universal tempered pro-semi-graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commensurably terminal properties of tempered subgroups (Corollary 6.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) π1^temp_G (viewed inside its profinite completion π1(G)) is commensurably terminal; (2) similarly for π1^temp_H for suitable sub-semi-graphs H. In particular π1^temp_H is commensurably terminal inside π1^temp_G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commensurably terminal means: elements of the ambient profinite group normalizing the tempered subgroup in a finite-index sense actually lie in the tempered subgroup; this controls conjugacy and normalizer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of X;H subgroups and cusps (Corollary 6.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given X and a connected sub-semi-graph H stabilized by GK, define π1^temp_{X;H} etc. Then: (1) π1^temp_{X;H} (resp. π1_{X;H}) is commensurably terminal in π1^temp_X (resp. π1_X); (2) closure of π1^temp_{X;H} in π1_X equals π1_{X;H}; (3) π1_{X;H} ∩ π1^temp_X = π1^temp_{X;H}; (4) an inertia subgroup I_x lies in the X;H-conjugate iff the corresponding cusp meets an irreducible component of the stable model contained in H; (5) under specific primes assumptions (p ∉ S and existence of l ∉ S ∪ {p,g?}) π1_{X;H} is slim; (6) similar commensurably terminal statements for tempered & profinite groups under primes assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This collects multiple technical structural properties about tempered/profinite subgroups attached to subgraphs, inertia placement, and slimness results used later; several items require prime-exclusion hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profinite Conjugates vs Tempered Conjugates (Theorem 6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Any inertia subgroup in π1_X of a cusp of X is contained in π1^temp_X iff it is an inertia subgroup in π1^temp_X of a cusp of X. (2) A π1_X-conjugate of π1^temp_X contains an inertia subgroup in π1^temp_X iff it is equal to π1^temp_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem is key for IUT: it shows that the profinite conjugacy indeterminacy of certain subgroups reduces to tempered conjugacy indeterminacy (harmless). Assumes p ∉ S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstruction of inertia and decomposition groups of cusps (Corollary 6.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a smooth hyperbolic log-curve X over K, one can reconstruct group-theoretically the inertia subgroups and the decomposition groups of cusps in π1^temp(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining Proposition 6.6 (identifying verticial/edge-like subgroups) and Theorem 6.11 removes profinite indeterminacies and allows identification of inertia/decomposition groups purely from π1^temp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of dual semi-graph and cyclotomic rigidity (Remark 6.12.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using reconstruction of the dual semi-graph of the special fibre, one can reconstruct (1) a positive rational structure on H^2(π1_X; Ẑ(GK))_ := Hom(H^2(π1_X; Ẑ(GK)), Ẑ), and (2) hence a cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (Cyc. Rig. via Pos. Rat. Str.) Ẑ(GK) → Ẑ(π1_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This outlines how combinatorial and cohomological reconstructions combine to yield cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms used in later parts of the theory; references to LCFT and further remarks are given.
